plan.question: Does the observed attention-by-count-normalization interaction repeat under the frozen protocol, or is it seed-specific optimization rather than evidence that learned target-aware attention compensates for behavior multiplicity? At seed 42, ordinary pooling has validation AUC 0.6102261137080656; full correction lowers it to 0.608492700295371, whereas half correction raises it to 0.6108065192309597. Ordinary DIN remains the incumbent at 0.6133619861190683; full and half correction reach 0.6131714801466076 and 0.6131537617707302 respectively, both with worse Logloss than ordinary DIN. The AUC interaction changes from +0.0015429074402 to -0.0007886298712 across full and half strength. Thus partial correction helps pooling in this seed but does not rescue DIN, and a uniformly beneficial compensation explanation is unsupported. First-512 candidate-authored diagnostics show active redistribution, not predictive relevance or a population mechanism. Retrieve prior open observations and nearest normalization work to determine a bounded discriminating follow-up: paired replication of existing arms if the host explicitly supports it, followed by mechanism-specific evidence only if warranted. Keep ordinary DIN as incumbent; no coefficient sweep or new subgroup gate follows from these summaries. This question concerns reproducibility and attribution, not a novelty claim.

observations.statement: The static, pooled and target-aware references have AUC 0.6050036145, 0.6102261137 and 0.6133619861. Pooling and target conditioning each improve both overall metrics at seed 42. Ordinary round-one controls exactly reproduce the corresponding reported reference metrics and slices.

All nine supplied trials succeeded operationally, including both latest arms. Full correction is a negative performance trajectory, not a failed execution: AUC falls by 0.0017334134 for pooling and 0.0001905060 for DIN, with worse Logloss in both. No failed execution receipt or additional abandoned branch is supplied.

Latest half-corrected pooling reaches AUC 0.6108065192 and Logloss 0.1969882654: changes of +0.0005804055 and -0.0000981980 against ordinary pooling. It recovers and exceeds the full-correction pooling penalty, but remains below ordinary DIN by 0.0025554669 AUC and has higher Logloss.

Latest half-corrected DIN reaches AUC 0.6131537618 and Logloss 0.1968125047: changes of -0.0002082243 and +0.0000178582 against ordinary DIN. Against full correction, AUC is lower by 0.0000177184 while Logloss improves by 0.0000135933. Thus half strength does not rescue the primary DIN objective in this seed.

The attention-by-correction AUC interaction is +0.0015429074 at full strength but -0.0007886299 at half strength. The original positive interaction does not extend uniformly over strength. DIN has a relatively flat three-point response while pooling is nonmonotonic; three points do not identify an optimum or response curve.

Latest candidate-supplied first-512 diagnostics show active alpha=0.5, zero padding mass, weight-sum error at most 2.3842e-7, zero empty summary, and near-invariant conditional within-type weights and single-type weights. Mixed-history mean half-versus-ordinary summary L2 changes are 1.0636960 for pooling and 1.1264205 for DIN. These support an active between-type redistribution in this limited sample, not a causal performance explanation.

At the half-DIN checkpoint, mean pv mass conditional on pv presence is 0.9295267 under ordinary normalization, 0.7707562 under half, and 0.4762428 under full correction. The corresponding half-pooling values are 0.9447256, 0.7888888 and 0.4281723. These are same-checkpoint counterfactual normalizations, not three retrained model performance measurements. Type-specific means use different presence denominators and must not be summed.

The diagnostic sample contains 4 empty, 40 single-type and 468 mixed-type histories; 395 mixed histories have at least 90% pv share. It is the first 512 ordered impressions, not a random population sample. Raw DIN score means differ across trained checkpoints and are not comparable evidence of compensation without centered, matched-input analysis.

Half pooling improves AUC and Logloss in each of four hour bins, but not every slice: past-buy-present AUC and the lowest user-frequency AUC decline. In category-match-absent impressions its AUC increases by 0.0009956346 while Logloss worsens by 0.0000363654. Half DIN instead loses category-absent AUC by 0.0004225199, reversing the full-DIN exploratory gain of 0.0003955323; Logloss worsens for both corrected DIN strengths in that slice.

Half DIN improves empty-history AUC by 0.0048421535 and Logloss by 0.0009431824 despite zero empty summaries in diagnostics. Such changes can arise through shared parameter training; they cannot be attributed to direct reweighting of empty histories. The slice has only 310 positive exposures. All three nonempty length bins have lower half-DIN AUC than ordinary DIN.

All six normalization arms report 17,130,275 parameters, including the unused attention module in pooling controls. Half pooling uses 455.44 training seconds and 430,361,088 peak GPU bytes; half DIN uses 491.36 seconds and 654,937,600 bytes. This is a matched-recipe/capacity comparison, not measured equal compute. Shorter round-two times occur in both branches and do not establish a correction-specific speedup.

interpretations.claim: Partial correction may trade useful behavior intensity against multiplicity in pooling, where full balancing overcorrects. The same primary-objective explanation is unsupported for DIN at seed 42.
interpretations.status: provisional; local controlled pooling signal, negative DIN evidence

interpretations.claim: Learned target-aware retrieval may reduce sensitivity to the explicit normalization strength, but the sign reversal of the interaction weakens a general claim that attention compensates beneficially for correction. Optimization, embedding geometry and score adaptation remain alternatives.

The intervention is numerically active and approximately preserves its intended conditional invariances in the diagnostic sample. Activity is separate from predictive usefulness, and sample-limited candidate diagnostics do not independently certify implementation correctness.

The original exploratory category-absent DIN gain has not generalized to half strength; it does not justify a subgroup gate, category/brand-specific architecture, or deployment rule. No observed query-construction or field-fusion bottleneck has been isolated.

memory_updates.statement: The prior half-strength rescue hypothesis has branch-dependent evidence: half pooling beats both pooling endpoints, while half DIN fails to recover full-DIN AUC and trails ordinary DIN. Preserve the original hypothesis and this qualification together.

The full-strength positive AUC interaction reverses at half strength. A general positive compensation interpretation is weakened; DIN flatness, optimization and seed variation remain competing explanations.
Half DIN reverses the full-strength category-absent AUC gain and still worsens Logloss. No stable subgroup mechanism or gate is supported.

limitations: Only seed 42 is measured. Aggregate summaries cannot yield paired user-cluster confidence intervals; identical bridge metrics do not supply independent repetitions.
The supplied diagnostics are candidate-authored, first-512 ordered impressions and not independently verified. Four empty and 40 single-type cases provide limited invariance checks.
Attention masses, score means and summary L2 changes do not establish event relevance, causal importance or performance mediation. Cross-checkpoint changes conflate retraining and normalization.

All slice analysis is exploratory. Counts are supplied in the complete slice table. No invented sufficiency threshold is imposed; empty-history (310 positives), pv-absent (397) and frequency-1_2 (1045) slices need particular caution. Positive exposure counts are not independent user counts.

Exact training-frequency interval semantics, history-length scope and category-match slice construction are not exposed. Diagnostic visible-window absence and scorer absence may differ. Missing/unseen-field performance slices are unavailable.
The model window is capped at 128 visible events. No claim is made about complete lifetime behavior, omitted events, or unavailable item identities.
AUC is not additive over slices. Improved slice AUC with worse Logloss alone does not diagnose probability calibration.

Model sources, checkpoints, raw data and training logs are absent. Historical readiness checks and source-note equivalence cannot be independently rerun here. Preparation notes saying untrained describe submission-time state; successful receipts establish subsequent execution.
Static user/ad snapshots have undocumented as-of dates. The frozen benchmark assumption is preserved; production point-in-time validity is unverified.

Parameter matching includes an unused pooling attention module, so it does not equalize active compute. Allocated GPU seconds and training examples processed are not supplied. Reported train/wall seconds and peak memory cannot replace those quantities. Batch p50/p95 includes causal feature gathering and is not per-request latency.
Single-run timings and differing checkpoint/round conditions cannot establish an equal-compute frontier or correction-specific speedup. No training was run in this phase.
All nine available trials succeeded; negative and qualified outcomes are retained. No unseen failure records, disabled personal memory or hidden trajectories are invented.

External nearest normalization literature and full primary papers were not inspected here. Provenance cards are not scientific verification. Novelty, priority and exact literature reproduction remain unverified.

Remaining budget is a runtime snapshot, not independently refreshed host accounting. The future plan is conditional on an authorized interface and available budget; it does not alter any frozen contract.
Only open validation was used. No test access, closed assessment, final checkpoint selection or reusable-holdout feedback occurred. Proposed memory updates contain only open evidence.

factorial_interaction.definition: (corrected DIN - ordinary DIN) - (corrected pool - ordinary pool)
factorial_interaction.interpretation: Attention attenuates the observed AUC penalty of full count correction. A positive AUC interaction does not mean corrected DIN beats ordinary DIN. The Logloss interaction is much smaller. This descriptive interaction has no estimated uncertainty.

observations.statement: History pooling improves AUC over static features by 0.0052224992242449, and target-aware attention improves over pooling by 0.0031358724110028. Both changes also lower overall Logloss. History and target conditioning therefore have local predictive value under this recipe.

Both ordinary arms reproduce their corresponding ancestors exactly in aggregate AUC, Logloss, and every reported slice metric, at identical parameter counts. This supports use of the ordinary arms as bridges for intervention attribution.

Full count correction lowers AUC and raises Logloss in both branches. The pooled penalty is -0.0017334134126946 AUC / +0.0000367396712915 Logloss; the DIN penalty is -0.0001905059724607 AUC / +0.0000314515662284 Logloss.
observations.outcome: negative for the proposed full-correction performance benefit

observations.statement: The AUC difference-in-differences is +0.0015429074402339. Target-aware scoring substantially attenuates the correction penalty in this seed; it does not reverse the overall ranking.

The diagnostic intervention is active: at the ordinary DIN checkpoint, mean pv attention mass conditional on pv presence changes from 0.829869 under ordinary weights to 0.323921 under corrected weights. The corrected-trained checkpoint has 0.965264 under ordinary counterfactual weights and 0.673296 under its active corrected weights. These are two normalizations per checkpoint; cross-checkpoint differences also include learned representation changes. Per-type reported means use different presence-conditioned denominators and must not be summed as a probability partition.
observations.scope: Candidate-supplied, first 512 validation impressions, not independently verified

observations.statement: Diagnostics cover 4 empty, 40 single-type and 468 mixed-type histories; 395/468 mixed histories have at least 90% pv events. Padding mass is zero and maximum normalization error is at most 2.3842e-7. Single-type summary perturbation is about 3e-7 to 4e-7 for DIN, consistent with subtracting a common log-count leaving softmax weights invariant. This is a narrow implementation sanity check, not population evidence or a relevance assessment.

Corrected DIN gains +0.0003955323 AUC on category_match_absent (717,129 samples / 29,616 positives / 687,513 negatives), while Logloss worsens by +0.0000537532; category_match_present loses -0.0003253239 AUC. The diagnostic category-absent subset also includes 16 brand-present histories among 134 nonempty category-absent histories. Category absence cannot be interpreted as absence of all useful evidence.

Corrected DIN loses -0.0015670382 AUC for history_1_16 and -0.0009893867 for history_17_64, but only -0.0000234989 for history_gt64. The longest slice contains 93.5849% of validation impressions. Global AUC includes cross-slice positive-negative pairs, so it cannot be decomposed as a sample-weighted sum of slice AUCs.

On empty histories corrected DIN improves +0.0019564707 AUC and -0.0017289143 Logloss, although the normalization has no direct event-weight intervention there. The 8,272 impressions contain only 310 positives. End-to-end retraining changes shared parameters, so empty/single-type cross-model changes do not establish a direct normalization effect.

Corrected DIN worsens AUC in the four supplied frequency groups below 100 and improves it by +0.0006541180 in the highest-frequency group, where Logloss worsens +0.0000913672. No calibration or frequency-specific mechanism is established by these aggregate divergences.

All seven supplied trials have success status and null errors. There is no supplied execution-failure or abandoned-implementation receipt. The unsuccessful scientific branches are full correction in pooling and full correction in DIN; they remain in the analysis. Baseline and bridge reruns use the same seed and do not constitute independent support.

interpretations.claim: Behavior multiplicity can dominate the normalization without being a harmful bias. Removing multiplicity changed summaries and hurt overall prediction in this setting.
alternatives: Useful intensity or composition information was removed from the aggregate.
Rare actions were upweighted despite weak or noisy target relevance.

interpretations.claim: Learned target-aware scores may compensate for, or be less sensitive to, the imposed count correction. The smaller DIN penalty and higher uncorrected pv mass in the corrected-trained model are consistent with adaptation.
interpretations.status: provisional; descriptive attention weights are not proof of causal relevance
alternatives: The correction acts as an optimization perturbation.
Different embedding geometry changes both scores and summary scale.
Seed-specific variation explains some or all of the small DIN gap.

interpretations.claim: The count-normalization mechanism was implemented sufficiently to perturb attention, but the causal claim that reducing frequent-action dominance improves full-population prediction lacks support. This does not refute all behavior-aware aggregation or a weaker correction.
interpretations.status: single-seed controlled negative result with limited diagnostics

interpretations.claim: Category-absent AUC gains and improved rare-action-absent slices motivate questions rather than subgroup deployment or a new architecture. AUC/Logloss disagreement, overlapping groups and small diagnostic subsets leave the relevance mechanism unresolved.

alternatives.explanation: Sampling and initialization variation could reverse the small DIN difference.
alternatives.discriminating_evidence: Paired seeds 43 and 44 for ordinary, partial and full corrected DIN; paired user-cluster intervals only if the host authorizes access to the necessary identities/predictions.

alternatives.explanation: Total visible count is a useful reliability or behavior-intensity cue, rather than purely unwanted multiplicity.
alternatives.discriminating_evidence: A predeclared partial-count correction tests overcorrection without adding inputs or capacity. A later explicit-count replacement would need a separate prospective plan and matched extra-feature controls; it is not included here.

alternatives.explanation: Target-irrelevant rare actions acquire too much mass.
alternatives.discriminating_evidence: At the same frozen checkpoints compare category/brand match-conditioned mass and summary perturbations under ordinary, half, and full normalization. This measures behavior, not labels or relevance ground truth. Do not equate category absence with irrelevance.

alternatives.explanation: Training dynamics, calibration shifts or representation rescaling explain the observed differences.
alternatives.discriminating_evidence: Distinguish same-checkpoint normalization effects from separately retrained models; request per-epoch learning/validation summaries only through a future authorized interface, and preserve the fixed epochs/optimizer.

alternatives.explanation: The first 512 ordered impressions may misrepresent overall behavior composition.
alternatives.discriminating_evidence: Representative deterministic diagnostics would be needed before population claims. If the host supports only the existing first-512 interface, retain that scope explicitly.

cost_analysis.interpretation: Full correction changes neither reported parameter capacity nor training recipe. DIN wall times are 603.198 vs 603.348 seconds and peak GPU bytes 655,593,472 vs 655,198,720. These tiny timing/memory differences from one run do not establish efficiency. Ordinary and corrected DIN throughputs are 186,963 and 191,635 examples/s; batch p95 latencies are 21.021 and 20.798 ms, including feature gathering, at batch size 4096. Batch latency is not per-request latency.
cost_analysis.ledger_caveat: The sum of supplied trial wall times is descriptive and is not the authoritative total resource debit. Preparation, diagnostics, calibration, failures and analysis also count. Use the host ledger; do not refund same-seed bridges or failed directions.

prior_work_and_difference.nearest_verified_local_reference: The frozen target-aware baseline and its ordinary DIN bridge.
prior_work_and_difference.inherited_components: Per receipt notes: existing static and history representations, target-aware scorer for DIN, softmax normalization, classifier, initialization/module construction, optimizer/loss, fields and causal history interface. These source-level claims cannot be independently checked without the sources.
prior_work_and_difference.proposed_and_tested_difference: For each valid visible event i of type b, replace its attention logit s_i by s_i - log(n_b), where n_b is the visible masked within-type count. With pooled scores this becomes equal mass per present type and uniform mass within type. With target-aware scores it normalizes each type total by its count; it does not force equal type masses.

next_action.action: Retain baseline-din; prepare a bounded partial-correction study for a later authorized experiment phase. Do not train or modify models during this analyze phase.
next_action.observation: Full correction substantially hurts pooling and slightly hurts DIN, despite active diagnostic changes; the smaller DIN penalty may indicate compensation or overcorrection.
next_action.mechanism_hypothesis: A fixed half-strength count correction preserves useful intensity while attenuating type multiplicity, avoiding some of the penalty of full correction. Target-aware scoring may account for the attenuation of the penalty.
next_action.nearest_existing_work: Use the ordinary and full-corrected local factorial as the immediate controls. Search and inspect primary work on behavior-wise normalization before asserting a literature difference; no priority claim is needed for this follow-up.
next_action.inherited_components: Keep existing embeddings, fields, history masks/limit, scorer, classifier, parameter construction/order, training recipe, initialization policy and causal boundaries.
next_action.proposed_difference: Use s_i - alpha*log(n_b), with one predeclared interior alpha=0.5 and existing endpoints alpha=0 and alpha=1. No learned gate, new count feature, history expansion or optimizer change.
controls_and_order: At seed 42, add only half-corrected pooling and half-corrected DIN. Reuse the four completed endpoint arms only after matching source/config/protocol/data identity and preserving parameter initialization order. This completes a descriptive attention-by-strength 2x3 comparison.

Run ordinary, half-corrected and full-corrected DIN at paired seeds 43 and 44 (six jobs). Together with seed 42 this estimates seed variation for the consequential DIN comparison. Pooling interaction remains single-seed unless a later predeclared repetition is justified.

For each checkpoint, retain the existing label-free normalization diagnostics and, if supported by the authorized interface, report ordinary/half/full weights at the same checkpoint to separate algebraic intervention from retraining. Preserve the first-512 caveat; do not assume a new sampling interface exists.
Do not introduce adaptive coefficients, additional variants or subgroup selection based on these results without a new prospective record. Never use withheld outcomes for continuation.
predicted_observations: Under a strength-related overcorrection explanation, alpha=0.5 should recover some of the alpha=1 AUC penalty while giving intermediate frequent-type mass at a fixed checkpoint.

A useful partial correction would beat alpha=0 on the primary validation objective with consistent paired-seed direction; a ranking-only gain with worse Logloss remains a tradeoff, not an unqualified benefit.
If target-aware scores compensate, DIN may show a flatter strength-response than pooling. This is a provisional interaction prediction, and it could also arise from optimization differences.
next_action.falsifying_evidence: Half correction does not recover the full-correction penalty, or ordinary DIN remains superior across paired seeds. A non-repeating interaction undermines the compensation explanation. Close the full-count-correction branch after this bounded study if neither mechanism nor performance is supported; retain all negative results.
next_action.selection_rule: Use validation only. Keep ordinary DIN unless a candidate has a better paired-seed primary result with uncertainty and Logloss tradeoffs reported. No p-value or user-cluster interval can be manufactured from aggregate metrics. Freeze the final source/config/checkpoint and comparison suite before any closed assessment.

cost.reserve_policy: Provisionally reserve three paired seeds for up to three frozen assessment models at full trial caps. Also leave the residual budget for preparation, diagnostics, attribution and failed attempts. These are planning bounds, not authorization, a budget increase, or a replacement for host accounting.

next_action.execution_prerequisites: A later runtime must authorize source editing and host experiment submission. Record source and config hashes, seed and all prospective controls before execution. If sources, seed control, diagnostics or remaining budget are unavailable, do not invent them or launch local training.
next_action.stop_rule: Respect the hard ledger and trial cap. Stop this branch after the bounded study if no useful signal survives; stop earlier if integrity cannot be maintained. The current analysis ends with this artifact and requests no test assessment.

scene_scoped_memory_updates.qualification: Single seed 42 only; no repeated support.
scene_scoped_memory_updates.observation: Both full-count-corrected variants lose full-population validation AUC and Logloss against their ordinary controls; attention reduces the AUC penalty. Ordinary DIN stays incumbent.

First-512 candidate-supplied diagnostics show active mass redistribution on mixed-type histories and near-invariance on single-type histories. Different checkpoints suggest possible adaptation but do not verify a mechanism.

limitations: Only seed 42 is available. Same-seed bridges are not independent repetitions; neither confidence intervals nor significance can be computed from these aggregate summaries.
The 512-impression diagnostics are candidate-supplied and ordered, with 4 empty and 40 single-type cases. They are not representative population estimates or independent measurement.
Attention mass and summary L2 changes do not establish event relevance, causal feature importance or a performance mechanism. Cross-checkpoint diagnostics confound retraining with the normalization.

Slice interpretations are exploratory; original prospective hypotheses and exact scorer bin definitions were not supplied. Counts are reported without an invented minimum-support cutoff. Small-positive slices, including empty and pv-absent histories, require particular caution; no slice is called confirmatory.

Category-match diagnostics and scorer category_match_absent may use different history scope/definitions. Only a 128-event model window is available; omitted older events cannot be inferred. Missing-brand and unseen-field performance slices were not supplied.
AUC is not additive over slices; cross-slice ranking changes may affect overall AUC. AUC/Logloss divergence alone does not diagnose calibration.

No model code, checkpoint hashes, raw inputs, per-sample predictions or cluster identifiers are available in this phase. Receipt notes support source claims only provisionally; source-level equivalence and causal audits have not been rerun.
Reported recipe/data identity are frozen. This analysis does not verify production point-in-time validity of static user/ad snapshots with undocumented dates.
Parameters are matched but compute differs by branch; single-run timing is noisy. Allocated GPU seconds, training examples processed and equal-compute results are absent.
All supplied attempts succeeded operationally. No unseen failures, omitted trajectories or disabled personal knowledge are invented. The two negative correction branches are retained.
Full primary papers and nearest normalization literature were not inspected in this analysis. No novelty, priority, exact DIN reproduction or industry-to-local transfer claim is made.
